events.text: Candidates for the imperial exam crowd every inn on the road to the capital.

choices.text: Share a room with a poor candidate

effects.log: He studies all night. You learn the classics by accident.
Scholars burn a lot of oil. (+6 taels)

events.text: A candidate begs you to smuggle notes into the exam hall.

effects.log: He curses you, then studies properly. He passes.
The examiners arrest three men.

events.text: Bandits rob a candidate of his travel money and his only brush.

ok.log: His money back, and his brush.

fail.log: The bandits escape. You lend him your own brush.

choices.text: Buy him a brush and a meal

effects.log: He writes your name in his first poem as an official. (−3 taels)

events.text: Outside the exam hall, candidates hold a poetry match to calm their nerves.

ok.log: They are surprised a fighter writes so well.

fail.log: Your verse is about a noodle. It gets a laugh.

effects.log: Every poem is secretly about fear.

events.text: A candidate from a powerful family wants a rival candidate hurt before the exam. He offers silver.

effects.log: The rival passes. He never forgets you.
You want no part of it.

events.text: Exam results go up on the wall. Crowds weep and cheer.

effects.log: Many will try again. You tell them so.
A night of toasts to new officials.

events.text: A scholar asks you to teach him to fight: 'Officials make enemies.'

effects.log: He teaches you to read legal documents in return.

choices.text: Tell him to hire a guard

effects.log: He hires you, for a month. (+10 taels)

events.text: Bookstalls near the exam hall sell everything: classics, poetry, and forbidden martial texts.

choices.text: Look for a real martial text

fail.log: A forgery. You notice before paying.

effects.log: The stall keeper sighs. You read half a book standing up.

events.text: Your tutor says if you study hard you can take the imperial exam one day.

effects.log: Your characters get straighter.
They do. Military ones. Your eyes light up.

events.text: The Temple of Literature, where candidates pray before the exam.

effects.log: May their brush be steady.

choices.text: Read the names of past top scholars

effects.log: Seven hundred years of brilliant, nervous people.

events.text: A scholar who failed for the tenth time sits drinking alone.

effects.log: He tells you what he really wanted to be: a sword master. It is not too late, you say.
Food helps everything a little.

events.text: A new official who remembers you from the exam road sends a letter with his seal: a favour, if ever you need one.

effects.log: A favour from an official is a rare thing.

choices.text: Ask him to help the poor in his district

effects.log: He does. For a while.
